Triangulation in Research: Types & Examples

Use triangulation whenever a question is too complex, contested or context-dependent to trust to a single method, and especially when you want to strengthen the validity of quantitative work or the trustworthiness of qualitative work. It is a cornerstone of robust mixed-methods and case-study designs.

Denzin distinguished four kinds of triangulation. They are not mutually exclusive — a single ambitious study may use several at once — but it helps to keep them conceptually separate so you can describe precisely what you did and why.
